to.implementation_strategy: NEW module core/model_manager.py as single writer: (1) source resolution (HF Hub / ModelScope / direct URL) reading config/model-catalog.json for license/open_weights/bundle_allowed fields; (2) download via huggingface_hub + hf_transfer with resume and sha256 verification; (3) cache layout product-forge/models/<provider>/<model>@<rev>/ (gitignored) with a models.lock JSON manifest (id, revision, size, sha256, license, fetched_at); (4) license gate blocking non-bundle-safe weights unless PF_ALLOW_RESTRICTED_WEIGHTS=1; (5) disk preflight (required size vs free space); (6) pack-scoped 'ensure only required modalities'; (7) CLI: python -m core.model_manager --list/--ensure/--verify/--prune. REUSE: config/model-catalog.json as the license/open_weights source of truth (extend it with bundle_allowed if absent); REUSE core/lock_manager.py only as a pattern reference for idempotent lock handling (it is a DB lock, not applicable directly); gates pattern from core/merge_gate.py for the license decision table. Tests use a fake source (no network) for unit level; one real small-model integration test.
dependency_findings: RELATED BI-0217 (BOM at packaging) - models.lock manifest fields (id, size, sha256, license) should align with the BOM schema.
REQUIRES nothing open; depends implicitly on config/model-catalog.json entries carrying license/open_weights/bundle_allowed (extend if missing).
Downstream: self-host adapters and packaging (BI-0214 destination-runtime triage) consume this capability later.
conflict_findings: core/model_manager.py claimed as single writer; no other open item creates this module.
Potential future conflict with BI-0217 which will read models.lock - read-only consumption, no write conflict.
Guard/merge-gate modules are listed as candidates but are unrelated writers; no overlap.
duplication_findings: No existing downloader/cache component among candidates; core/agent_model_override.py, core/cost_model.py, core/business_models_kb.py are model-metadata and cost modules, not fetchers.
core/lock_manager.py is a database advisory-lock helper, not a file-based download lock - pattern reuse only, not a duplicate.
BI-0217 (BOM/footprint artifact) will want models.lock data - RELATED, not duplicate; models.lock can feed the BOM.
No open backlog item implements model fetching; duplication risk low.
to.rationale: No reusable downloader exists; a single new owner module (core/model_manager.py) is justified as NEW_CAPABILITY, while catalog and gate patterns are reused. Idempotent ensure, license gating, and pack-scoped downloads directly unblock provider_kind=self-host and safe packaging.
assumptions: config/model-catalog.json can be extended with bundle_allowed and is the source of truth for license metadata.
Users can override the gate via PF_ALLOW_RESTRICTED_WEIGHTS=1.
huggingface_hub supports resume and exposes file-level sha256/revision info needed for the lock.
Self-host adapters will consume the cache path convention product-forge/models/<provider>/<model>@<rev>/.
risks: Network availability in CI for the integration test - mitigated by a tiny model (Piper voice/tesseract tessdata) and by faking the source in unit tests.
huggingface_hub/hf_transfer become new runtime dependencies - must be declared and license-checked.
HF Hub rate limits and mirror availability (ModelScope) may affect resolution reliability.
Catalog entries may lack license/open_weights/bundle_allowed fields today - gate would default-refuse; needs a catalog extension step.
Huge model sizes vs CI disk - mitigated by pack-scoping and disk preflight.
License data on HF can be inaccurate; trusting catalog curation is an assumption.
evidence: Candidate components are metadata/cost/gate modules - none implements download, confirming a new module is required.
config/model-catalog.json exists and is the natural license/open_weights source.
core/merge_gate.py and core/lock_manager.py demonstrate existing gate and idempotency patterns to mirror.
